manifest.name: dsh-agent-teams-model-override
manifest.description: Model selection, model switching, and real nested manager/worker teams for DeepSeek Harness Agent Teams.
manifest.author: funk80rus (https://github.com/funk80rus)

bundle.text:
# Three REAL Cordis rows: separate fibers, tools, authority and UI switches.
# All entries select the SAME complete immutable graph. Never add these rows
# directly to the profile patch (that would bypass bundle disable).
- insert:
    - id: agent-teams-model-override
      name: './runtime/d7e10f8a9310ec39ec5a/plugin.js'
      config:
        force: false
        rosterModel: true
    - id: agent-teams-manager
      name: './runtime/d7e10f8a9310ec39ec5a/manager-component.js'
      config:
        nestedTeams: true
    - id: agent-teams-teammate-model
      name: './runtime/d7e10f8a9310ec39ec5a/teammate-model.js'
      config:
        switchModel: true

readme.text:
1. **Model selection when a teammate is created** — `spawn_teammate_with_model` accepts
   `provider`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort`; the teammate keeps that route across later
   turns and cold resume. The roster reports the session's real model instead of the profile
   default.
2. **Real nested teams** — a manager can create its own workers with a genuine
   `Session.header.parentSession = manager`, share the Lead's task board, delegate work inside
   its own zone, and interrupt its own workers. Nested transcripts open from the Team panel.
3. **Model switching for a live teammate** — `switch_teammate_model` changes the route of an
   existing teammate on its next request without creating a new member or losing its history.

It is a thin extension of the official Agent Teams bundle. It does not implement a second
orchestrator, copy board transitions, or replace the native continuable-subagent lifecycle.
When the official `spawn_teammate` learns these arguments itself, this package can go away.

> **Status: 1.6.0.** 201 tests pass against DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`. The creation/model paths are
> live-verified. The 1.6.0 manager-interrupt and nested-transcript paths are covered by
> contract tests against the installed runtime; a live UI pass is still pending, so treat
> those two paths as release-candidate behavior.

---

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek Harness | Desktop `0.2.1-rc.2` (tested), `0.2.0-rc.2` also supported |
| Official bundle | **Agent Teams** installed and enabled |
| Node.js | 22+ (development only; the installed Host provides its own runtime) |
| Profile | any; the package is a normal DSH bundle |

The plugin checks private runtime seams before installing. If the installed DSH no longer
matches the contracts it was written against, the affected component **refuses to install**
and writes the reason to the Host log instead of failing in the middle of a turn.

---

1. Make sure the official **Agent Teams** bundle is installed and enabled.
2. Open **Plugin Manager** in Creator Mode and choose **Install bundle**.
3. Enter the GitHub spec:

```text
   github:funk80rus/dsh-agent-teams-model-override
   ```

4. Enable `dsh-agent-teams-model-override`. Three component rows appear in **Components**;
   each row has its own toggle:

| Component | What it adds |
   | --- | --- |
   | `agent-teams-model-override` | `spawn_teammate_with_model`, accurate roster model |
   | `agent-teams-manager` | `spawn_team_worker`, zone task delegation, manager interrupt, nested transcripts |
   | `agent-teams-teammate-model` | `switch_teammate_model` for a running teammate |

The committed `runtime/<hash>/` graph is what the Host loads. A GitHub install does **not**
need a build step.

```bash
DSH_HOME="${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}"
PROFILE="$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>"          # e.g. desktop
cd "$PROFILE"

Then enable the bundle through the Plugin Manager UI, or from a DSH session:

```text
plugin_manager { action: "set_bundle", target: "dsh-agent-teams-model-override", enabled: true }
```

If `pnpm` refuses a fresh git dependency because of a release-age policy, install it through
the Plugin Manager instead, or pass `--config.minimumReleaseAge=0` for that one command.

The package is **not published to npm** and is marked `"private": true`; GitHub is the
distribution channel.

---

readme.text:
Ask the Host which routes are eligible first:

```text

```

readme.section: Pick a model for a new teammate
readme.text:
* `provider` and `model` must be supplied together. `reasoning_effort` is optional and is
  validated against the efforts that model actually advertises.
* Omit all three to inherit the delegating agent's route exactly as official
  `spawn_teammate` does.
* A route that is unknown or not allowed by the profile's subagent model allowlist is
  refused with an explicit error; it never silently falls back to the parent model.
* The model choice grants **no additional delegation authority**. Limits, depth, member
  slots, and tool permissions are unchanged.

```text
// Lead: create a manager with the normal or model-aware tool
spawn_teammate({ name: "mg-1", description: "Release manager", prompt: "..." })

// mg-1, from its own scope:

The Lead can also choose the real parent explicitly:

```text
spawn_teammate_with_model({ name: "w-2", ..., manager: "mg-1" })
```

Assign and track work:

```text
team_task_assign({ subject: "Fix the parser", description: "...", owner: "w-1" })
team_task_list({})
team_task_update({ task_id: "task-7", expected_revision: 2, action: "complete" })
team_hierarchy({})

A manager may change tasks only inside its **actual** descendant zone (computed from durable
`parentSession` headers, not from declared labels). Outside that zone the call fails with
`TEAM_TASK_OUT_OF_ZONE`; `claim` is never widened, and the Lead is not affected.

```text
interrupt_agent({ target: "w-1" })
```

A manager may interrupt only its own descendants; the Lead may interrupt anyone. The native
`interrupt` operation is still executed as the real Lead after the zone check, so the
official semantics are preserved: the current turn stops, pending inbox/activation survive,
and the next message starts the worker again. Self-interrupt returns
`TEAM_INTERRUPT_SELF`; an unrelated target returns `TEAM_INTERRUPT_OUT_OF_ZONE`.

readme.section: Switch the model of a running teammate
readme.text:
```text
switch_teammate_model({
  target: "w-1",
  provider: "opencode-go",
  model: "qwen3.8-flash"

The member keeps its id, name, history, journal entry, and board tasks. Only its next request
uses the new route. The official session controller appends the durable
`model/selection` event, so the change survives cold resume. The response says which path
was used:

readme.section: Switch the model of a running teammate

readme.text:
All three rows are inserted by `cordis.patch.yml` and select the **same immutable graph**
`runtime/<hash>/`, so component versions can never drift apart.

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: agent-teams-model-override
      name: './runtime/<hash>/plugin.js'
      config: { force: false, rosterModel: true }

* `force` — install even when the route seam is missing (not recommended; the component will
  be unable to deliver a route).
* `rosterModel` — replace only the `model` field of roster rows with the session's effective
  model.
* `nestedTeams` — enable real nested managers/workers and the zone task/interrupt authority.
* `switchModel` — register `switch_teammate_model`.

Disabling a row removes its tools and shadows immediately. Disabling the manager row does not
break already-created nested members while another row is still loaded; the read/recovery
bridge is reference-counted.

**Do not add these rows to the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml`.** A profile-level insert
would keep the plugin alive after `set_bundle(enabled: false)` and make the bundle impossible
to disable cleanly. Use only the package's `cordis.patch.yml`, which the bundle loader
applies.

---

* **Route injection is per call.** The selected route lives in an `AsyncLocalStorage` store
  created by one tool call and is consumed exactly once by the first `startContinuable` /
  `startActivation` whose parent is that delegating agent. Nothing global is mutated.
* **Nested creation reuses the official admission path.** The bridge calls the original
  `roster.spawn` as the real Lead (name checks, member limit, journal root, provisioning),
  then rewrites `request.parent` to the manager immediately before the native start. The
  child gets a real `parentSession`, the manager's catalog, and the shared team journal/board.
* **Zones come from actual lineage.** Task and interrupt authority is computed from
  `parentSession` headers, not from decorative hierarchy records. A manager cannot grant
  itself authority over another manager's children.
* **Nested transcript opening is a read-side repair.** The Team panel asks for history with
  `parent = Lead`; for a nested worker the durable parent is the manager, so the Host rejects
  it as `subagent/unauthorized`. The component wraps only `sessionController.page` and
  `follow`: if the supplied parent is a real ancestor of the actual par

1. **Private runtime seams.** Nested teams depend on the installed Agent Teams/subagent
   internals (`roster.spawnAdmitted`, activation registry, delivery symbol, session
   controller). A future DSH that changes them makes the component fail closed with a reason
   in the Host log. It is not a promise of forward compatibility.
2. **No teammate deletion or renaming.** The official roster is append-only. A `failed`
   creation still consumes its name and slot. A Lead session has 16 teammate slots
   (the Lead is separate); `context: "fresh"` creates a new member, it does not reuse one.
3. **No true context clear.** `/compact` in the GUI summarizes history; it does not erase it.
   The only clean start is a new teammate with `context: "fresh"`. There is no `/clear` tool
   for teammates in 1.6.0.
4. **A nested worker replies to its manager,** not to the Lead. That is the consequence of a
   real `parentSession`. Use an explicit `send_message({ target: "lead" })` when the worker
   must answer the Lead.
5. **Pending model switches are in memory.** If the Host restarts between
   `switch_teammate_model` returning `via: "pending"` and the teammate's next start, repeat
   the switch.
6.

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| No new tools after enabling | Is the official Agent Teams bundle enabled? Is the package bundle enabled? Did the component log a `runtimeSupportReport` failure? |
| `TEAM_LEAD_REQUIRED` from a manager | The `agent-teams-manager` row is disabled or failed to install. |
| `TEAM_INTERRUPT_OUT_OF_ZONE` | The target is not a real descendant of the caller. Check `team_hierarchy`. |
| `subagent/unauthorized` when opening a nested transcript | Confirm `agent-teams-manager` is enabled at 1.6.0+; this is the read-side repair. |
| Model did not change | Look at `via` and `warning` in the response. `session-append` means the official commit path was unavailable. |
| Install fails in `pnpm` | Use the Plugin Manager, update Node to 22+, or retry without a release-age policy for the git dependency. |
| Tools disappeared after a DSH update | The private contracts changed; check the Host log for the fail-closed reason. |

```bash
npm test          # 201 tests; installed-runtime tests skip when DSH is not found
npm run build     # writes lib/ into runtime/<hash>/ and rewrites exports + patch
npm run verify    # build, then the full suite
```

* `DSH_ASAR` can point at a non-default `app.asar`; the test helpers otherwise look for
  `/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar`.
* **Never edit `runtime/<hash>/` by hand.** It is content-addressed. Change `lib/`, run
  `npm run build`, then commit the new graph together with the updated `package.json` and
  `cordis.patch.yml`.
* The package has no runtime dependencies; tests use Node's built-in test runner.
* Keep local logs, profile snapshots, session ids, and absolute home paths out of commits.
  `.gitignore` already excludes `.diagnostics/`, `docs/evidence/`, `docs/rollback/`, and the
  author's internal notes.

Contributions are welcome; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

---

The plugin runs inside the local DSH Host with the user's permissions. It makes **no network
requests** of its own, has no telemetry, and does not read credentials or API keys. It reads
local session headers and the official services to compute lineage, routes, and history
addresses; that data stays on the machine.

It does hook private runtime seams, so treat it as privileged local code: install from a
commit you trust, and read [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) before reporting a vulnerability.
